🇵🇰 MARYAM NAWAZ GOVERNMENT’S SIX-MONTH DEVELOPMENT REPORT — 20 MAJOR PUBLIC WELFARE PROJECTS ACROSS PUNJAB

May–November 2026 | Punjab, Pakistan

Over the past six months, the Punjab government, led by Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif, has announced, launched, approved or advanced a range of development and public welfare initiatives across the province.

1. Apni Chhat, Apna Ghar Housing Scheme
Interest-free housing loans continued to support low-income families seeking to build their own homes.

2. Apni Zameen, Apna Ghar
The government continued its housing support initiatives aimed at helping deserving families access affordable homes.

3. Electric Bikes for Students
On October 16, an initiative was announced to provide 100,000 electric bikes to students during the year.

4. Sahiwal Development Package
Four development projects worth Rs5.61 billion were inaugurated in Sahiwal on October 16.

5. Sahiwal Sports Arena
A modern sports facility was inaugurated to provide improved sporting opportunities for young people.

6. Sahiwal–Arifwala Road
A 27-kilometre road development project was included in the region's major infrastructure initiatives.

7. Faisalabad Ring Road
Five major road development projects, including the Faisalabad Ring Road, were launched on October 4.

8. Narowal Road Infrastructure
Road improvement projects covering Muridke–Narowal and Shakargarh–Narowal were included in the development programme.

9. AI-Powered Cleanliness Monitoring
Artificial intelligence technology was introduced to improve monitoring and management of sanitation services across Punjab.

10. Development of Katcha Areas
A Rs23 billion development package was announced in May to improve infrastructure and basic facilities in riverine communities.

11. Electric Bus Services
Expansion of environmentally friendly public transport services, including initiatives in Attock and other districts, remained part of the government's transport agenda.

12. Clean Drinking Water
Clean drinking water initiatives continued to receive attention, with a focus on improving access to safe water across Punjab.

13. Lab on Wheels for Farmers
Mobile agricultural laboratories were introduced to provide farmers with modern testing facilities and technical guidance.

14. Modern Agricultural Machinery
The High-Tech Farm Mechanization Finance Programme aimed to improve farmers' access to modern agricultural equipment.

15. Special Education for Children
The Maryam Nawaz School and Resource Centre for Autism announced the admission of 72 additional children in its second phase, providing education and therapy facilities.

16. Free Healthcare Initiatives
Health Week activities in May provided free medical examinations and screening services for conditions including diabetes and high blood pressure.

17. Green Railway Corridor
A Green Railway Corridor initiative was inaugurated as part of efforts to address environmental pollution and smog.

18. Ramazan Nigehban Welfare Programme
Financial assistance and ration support initiatives continued to target deserving and low-income families.

19. Road Infrastructure and Maintenance
Five major road projects included plans for construction, private-sector participation and a seven-year maintenance framework.

20. Urban Development Projects
Work continued on improving drainage, sewerage systems, roads and essential municipal infrastructure in different districts under Punjab's development programmes.

---

PUBLIC DEVELOPMENT AND SERVICE DELIVERY

These initiatives cover housing, healthcare, education, agriculture, transportation, sanitation and infrastructure. Their actual impact will ultimately depend on timely completion, transparent spending and effective delivery of services to ordinary citizens.

Important clarification: This report covers projects announced, approved, inaugurated or advanced during the stated period. It does not imply that all 20 projects have been fully completed or delivered.

text:
🌊 OUR RIVERS ARE DYING. OUR VOICES WILL NOT BE SILENCED. THE FIGHT TO SAVE PUNJAB'S RIVERS HAS BEGUN! 🌊

The fight to save Punjab's rivers is no longer just an environmental concern; it is a fight for our water, our health, our future generations and the very survival of Punjab.

On 1 November, environmentalists, social activists, farmers' representatives and concerned citizens from across Punjab came together in Jalandhar at a meeting convened by Chitti Bein Morcha to discuss the alarming pollution of Kala Sanghian, Chitti Bein and the Sutlej.

The participation and commitment shown by everyone was truly encouraging. Several important decisions were taken, including:

🔹 Formation of a democratic state-level member committee to coordinate the movement.

🔹 Formation of regional committees in all affected villages to ensure grassroots participation.

🔹 Taking the fight forward through legal action, public awareness campaigns and ground-level protests.

🔹 Opposing industries across Punjab that violate environmental laws, particularly polluting Red Category industries.

One thing was made absolutely clear: We cannot keep treating our rivers as dumping grounds for industrial waste. Heavy metals and other toxic contaminants pose serious challenges to water quality and public health. Cleaning polluted water after contamination is extremely difficult. The only sustainable solution is to stop pollution at its source.

Governments may change, but the pollution continues. We cannot afford to remain silent any longer. This movement will remain democratic, non-partisan and united by one common objective — saving Punjab's rivers.

A BIG THANK YOU TO THE MEDIA!

We are extremely grateful to all newspapers and media organisations that covered this meeting and helped bring this critical environmental issue to the forefront.

A special and heartfelt thanks to Ashwani Khurana Ji and Aparna Banerji Ji for their fearless green journalism and for consistently highlighting environmental issues that deserve public attention. Independent and courageous journalism is indispensable in holding those responsible accountable.

My sincere thanks also to Jugal Kishore Ji, Sehgal Ji, Parveen Kumar Ji, Kapil Ji, Jaspal Ji, Shiv Sharma Ji, Vikas Sharma Ji and everyone else who is contributing, supporting and standing with us in this fight to protect our environment.

To all the environmentalists, activists, organisations and citizens who attended the meeting — thank you for your time, commitment and solidarity.

This is bigger than any individual or organisation. We may have different ideologies and backgrounds, but our rivers, our water and our future are common.

Let us remain united. Let us remain fearless. Let us not allow any divisive forces to weaken this movement.

The next generation deserves clean rivers, not a legacy of toxic water.
